content: This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as those measuring sex hormone-binding globulin or thyroid function, potentially leading to inaccurate test results. If you suspect an overdose and the individual exhibits severe symptoms like loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). For non-emergency situations, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, while Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. It is essential to undergo regular comprehensive physical examinations, including laboratory and medical tests such as blood pressure monitoring, breast exams, pelvic exams, and Pap smears, while taking this medication. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and promptly report any lumps. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, refer to the product’s package information for specific guidance. You may need to use additional birth control methods, such as condoms or spermicides, to prevent pregnancy. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into drains unless explicitly instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Common side effects of this medication may include nausea, vomiting, headache, bloating, breast tenderness, or weight gain. Vaginal bleeding between periods (spotting) or missed/irregular periods may also occur. If these effects persist or worsen, inform your doctor or pharmacist promptly. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. For medical advice about side effects, contact your doctor. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to norethindrone, other progestins, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on your face and skin (melasma), which can be worsened by sunlight. Limit sun exposure, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It can pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some drugs may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control by decreasing the levels of birth control hormones in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (such as rifampin, rifabutin), ritonavir, and St. John’s Wort. Inform your doctor when starting any new medication and discuss whether you should use reliable backup birth control. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as those measuring sex hormone-binding globulin or thyroid function, potentially causing false test results. Always inform your healthcare provider and laboratory personnel that you are using this medication.
